entries.entry: Alright, here goes. --- 1st January 2020. Happy New Year, I guess? It's freezing today, proper Sheffield weather, damp and grey. Not the best start to a new year, if I'm honest. Looking back at friendships, I feel a bit all over the place. Like, where are my mates? Everyone's busy with their lives, and it just feels a bit lonely. I read some self-help book last month, but the takeaways just reminded me how disconnected I feel. It's frustrating. Then there's resilience. I had my challenges in 2019, but every time I think I've bounced back, something else whacks me down. Can't shake off this nagging feeling of not quite being where I want to be. Relationships are tough too, like figuring out what emotional intelligence even means when you can't get a response back from someone for days. It's like... am I doing it wrong? I visited this cute café yesterday; Sophie and I went for a post-holiday catch-up. The vibe was lovely, but I regretted not spending more time there. It was bittersweet, really. Online, things aren't great either. The constant scrolling just reminds me of all the places I haven't been and the friends I'm missing. But then there's Goldie. My little fish. Weirdly, he brings me joy. Just watching him swim, it's like he's got his little world sorted. And I had a good chat with my mentor the other day. He's always so uplifting. Honestly, those moments of pride and gratitude stand out amidst everything else. So, here's to 2020. I guess it can only get better?

**Wednesday, 1st January 2020** So, it's the New Year, and honestly, feeling a bit rubbish about my yoga. I thought I'd be bending like a pretzel by now, but nope, just me and my inflexible body. As for travel, still dreaming of Bali, while my bank account is grim. Reflecting on last year's mistakes, I can't help but feel a bit embarrassed. A friend dropped by with her dog today, though, and that brought me pure joy! He just flopped down on my lap, proper cute. Did some volunteering too—helping out at the local shelter felt brilliant. Gaming lately has been a laugh; I finally beat my mate in FIFA (yes!). Cooking's been a mixed bag; can't get that risotto right, but finding old childhood photos brought back some sweet memories. Balancing everything's tricky, but I'm grateful for my people. Here's to more!

Alright, let's get this down. So, it's Thursday, 02 January 2020, and honestly, I'm feeling a bit off today. I dunno, maybe it's the grey, miserable weather in Sheffield; it's dull and rainy, which always seems to dull my mood. Creative writing has just been a massive flop lately. Ideas that used to spark joy now just feel like chores, ya know? I tried sitting down with my notebook, but all I managed was to scribble a few half-hearted lines. Frustrating! And about society—it's like I'm stuck in this loop of negativity. The way the world is going, it's easy to get lost in the crowd of terrible news and social media rubbish. Not great for my mental space. Then there's this whole fitness thing I'm trying to juggle. I had hoped to kick off the year strong, but the lack of motivation is hitting hard. On a brighter note, I did explore badminton a bit more, and it's turned out to be a proper laugh. My mate Tom came by yesterday, and we both had a right giggle trying to practice juggling a few times. I actually managed to keep the ball in the air for a solid minute, which felt brilliant! But then, there were a few awkward moments with someone I fancied. It was a bit cringe at first, but there's something oddly comforting about being vulnerable. Just a mix of excitement tinged with the worry of rejection. Had a lovely chat with Grandma Helen, though; she always knows how to lift my spirits. Anyway, here's to hoping tomorrow's a bit brighter.

Right, so it's January 2nd, and honestly, it's been a pretty mixed bag today. The weather's typical for Sheffield—bleak with this annoying drizzle. I went to train, but I'm feeling really off about my calisthenics goals. I just can't seem to progress, and it's getting me down. I thought I'd be further along by now, but it just feels like a slog. On a brighter note, work's been decent. We had this brainstorming session, and I actually contributed a lot. It felt good to be heard. Plus, I caught up with mates for a cheeky pint later, and those laughs always lift my spirits. Family's been great too. Spent time with my younger brother. He's so brilliant, watching him just makes me feel proud. I've got that notebook for gratitude journaling. Today I wrote about small wins—a little self-care ritual I've started. It helps with the mixed feelings about everything else. Travel dreams are still floating about too. Just wish I could get there without all this pressure hanging over me. Ah well, onwards and upwards, I suppose.
